summary: This standards-track memo updates the required and suggested algorithms for Internet Key Exchange version 1. The original specification allowed weak security and suggested algorithms that were rarely implemented, so this document aligns it with market needs.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4109 updates the algorithms that IKEv1 implementations are required or advised to support. It makes some choices stronger requirements and lowers weak or little-used choices to optional.

questions: which diffie-hellman group is mandatory in ikev1
what does rfc 4109 change in rfc 2409
subtitle: Updated requirements for the cryptographic algorithms supported by IKEv1 implementations.

tldr.problem: The original IKEv1 requirements included weak algorithms and choices that were not widely implemented.
tldr.mechanism: The memo changes which algorithms IKEv1 implementations MUST, SHOULD or MAY support, including stronger requirements for TripleDES and Diffie-Hellman group 2.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4109 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 2409 and drops several algorithms to MAY.

today: RFC 4109 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 2409. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes RFC 4109.

sections.title: Why the IKEv1 List Changed
sections.content: The original IKEv1 specification, RFC 2409, required and recommended algorithms that the memo says did not match IPsec users' needs. It allowed weak security and suggested algorithms that were thinly implemented. RFC 4109 updates those algorithm requirements for IKEv1 implementations.
sections.plainLanguage: The old IKEv1 algorithm list included weak choices and choices that were rarely implemented. This memo changes which algorithms implementations must or should support.

sections.title: The New Support Requirements
sections.content:
Implementations MUST support TripleDES for encryption, SHA-1 for hashing and HMAC, pre-shared secrets for authentication, and Diffie-Hellman MODP group 2. They SHOULD support AES-128 in CBC mode for encryption, AES-128 in XCBC mode for PRF functions, Diffie-Hellman MODP group 14, and RSA signatures.

DES, MD5 and MODP group 1 move to MAY because of cryptographic weakness. Tiger, elliptic-curve groups, DSA signatures and RSA encryption move to MAY because of limited deployment and interoperability.
sections.plainLanguage: Every implementation must support the listed required algorithms. Other choices are recommended, while weak or little-used choices become optional.

sections.title: Security and Future Changes
sections.content: The RFC says that the algorithms in its new MUST and SHOULD requirements were believed robust and secure at the time it was written. It also says that if IKEv1 receives further updates, AES-128 in CBC mode will very likely become mandatory for encryption.
sections.plainLanguage: The authors considered the required and recommended algorithms robust when they wrote the memo. They expected AES-128 in CBC mode might become mandatory in a later IKEv1 update.
